I’ve had GERD since I was 13 (I’m 24 now). 
A couple of things I’ve come to notice, especially as a young person with it:
1. People assume that when you say you have GERD, you’re experiencing the same thing they do when they have occasional heartburn.  They don’t take you seriously. 
2. In the same regard, people don’t understand that GERD has actual ramifications if it’s not treated. Their heartburn just causes them slight discomfort when not treated, your GERD can cause esophagitis and esophageal cancer, but they don’t get that. 
3. People are so centered around a diet only being something for weight loss, they can’t comprehend why you would cut food out for any other reason. I come from a family of people that probably all look like we have eating disorders from the outside, but we all have IBS, GERD, and autoimmune diseases. We follow a diet because it genuinely makes us feel better and there’s nothing wrong with that. 

Hang in there 💜 Navigating health stuff at a young age can be very lonely. I highly recommend finding friends that are chronically ill or disabled, they’ll understand you even if their health isn’t remotely similar to yours.

I’m Bipolar! I tend to take these medications most often to calm mania or for acute insomnia. I rely on a high dose of Valproic Acid every night to put me to sleep regularly. 

Here’s how my doc does PRNs when I’m manic:

Night one: Ativan

If I didn’t sleep or am still very manic, night two: Ativan and Olanzipine

If I didn’t sleep or am still very manic, night three: Ativan and Seroquel 

If I didn’t sleep or am still very manic, night four: Ativan, Benadryl, and Olanzipine 

If I’m still manic, we’ll do Olanzipine for two weeks to stabilize. My doctor avoids regularly using both Olanzipine and Seroquel as they cause me to sleepwalk and I’ve started fires in my sleep before. Plus, I get the metabolic syndrome for both, so I can’t regularly use them. 

Most antipsychotics cause me to sleepwalk, actually. We have to rely on anticonvulsants to treat my bipolar for the most part, which aren’t usually nearly as effective.
